_comment: A reply's text pieces and what a binding makes of their <think> blocks (CON288 (b)). Owner decision 2026-11-21 (D5): one contract with two outputs, answer for display by OxidANT's per-block rule and final for grading by the lab's rule; text before a late </think> in the same piece is not shown, as the web shows it. Owner decision 2026-11-23: final stops at a <think> that opens after the last </think> and never closes.
events: pieces arrive in order. shown is everything given out while they stream, joined: text that may still begin a tag waits for the next piece, white space right after a closing tag is dropped, and a late </think> (one without its opening, which a chat template wrote into the prompt) hides the text before it in its own piece, while text an earlier piece showed stays shown. answer is the visible answer at the end: text outside blocks, less that white space, and a late close turns all answer before it into thinking. final is the joined text after the last </think>, up to a <think> that opens after it; with no </think> it is the whole text, or empty when a <think> opened. thinking counts the characters of the blocks, their tags and the answer a late close took back; late_closes counts closing tags without their opening

cases.name: one block, and the white space after it is no answer
several blocks: the answer joins what lies between them, final is after the last
text before <think> is answer, but not final
an unclosed block after an answer
a block that never closed has neither answer nor final
a late close inside one piece hides the text before it
a late close in a later piece leaves shown what was shown
a second close after a block is late
a < in the answer is held back, then shown
